entries.reason: Curated area mapping; the named test asserts this behaviour.

DeltaPlasticAdapter implements the PlasticAdapter contract with projection/state init and dimension validation.
Rank-one gated Delta Rule: S <- S + beta * outer(k, v - S^T k), beta = sigmoid(W_beta x).
Householder-reflected erase with bounded attenuation and a before/after/collateral report.
Versioned delta/sparse state; newer versions and mismatched geometry are rejected, legacy associative profiles still load.
Covers zero/full beta, repeated writes, value overwrite, selective erase and unrelated-key preservation.
SparseCoder: 384-D input, 2048-D latent, deterministic TopK-128, reconstruction and utilization metrics.
SparseDeltaAdapter composes the coder with the delta core; FlyModelAdapter keeps the same PlasticAdapter API.
delta_rtu, sparse_delta and fly_model are registered; discovery, unknown-name errors and profile serialization are tested.
Exact 2048-D code, exactly 128 active entries, 93.75% sparsity, stable ties and round-trip shape.
New profiles may select delta_rtu; existing profile metadata still selects associative_rtu.
Teaching and recall go through the adapter contract; the default profile keeps associative_rtu until migration is selected.
docs/delta-migration.md documents selection, re-teaching migration, rollback and incompatibility behavior.
Versioned 20-task protocol with fixed seeds, fixed task order, fixed splits and scoring.
Budget-matched EWC reference (one Fisher pass + one step per pattern) with a documented memory-loss formula.
Measured per-task loss, interference, latency and code utilization; delta memory loss 0.1198 missed the <0.10 target and is published as a miss.
Full configuration and per-task results are published; the ~0.24 EWC reference is labelled a target and was not reproduced.
Adapter, DroidEngine, checkpoint and profile suites pass (621 passed, 1 skipped).
Full suite green and old associative_rtu checkpoints still load.

Sparse-code memory and encode latency measured: 128 active entries per row (262144 B of float32 codes per row), traced peak 176.0 KiB for a 512-row batch, encode p50 6.166 ms; the dense/sparse update latency, retrieval quality and interference rows are published in reports/evidence/2026-10-21-delta-benchmark.json.
autonomous_retrieval() is driven only by internal memory state plus a decaying self-inhibition trace.
Replay step/time/confidence/cancellation/duplicate controls are implemented and tested.
DroidEngine.sleep() returns status, duration, coverage, replay and pruning counts plus errors.
consolidate_memory() is invoked separately from fact and parameter pruning, whose counts stay distinct in the report.
Fixed correlated-pattern fixture and a 100-pattern benchmark recover all 100 patterns with no expected list passed in.
MAS importance uses the squared-L2 output objective with exactly one backward pass per sampled batch.
Eligible parameters are limited to plastic weights; the frozen anchor and buffers are excluded.
Lowest-importance 10% is pruned deterministically (floor) with importance scores and reversible masks persisted.
Ranking, single backward pass, exact prune count, checkpoint round trip and allowlist scope are covered.
Retrieval quality is sampled before and after pruning; a regression is reported with a warning instead of hidden.
lr_i = base_lr * decay_factor^i with zero-based index and validated bounds.
Schedule index and effective rate are stored in the profile and restored on load.
Monotonicity, bounds, restart continuity and optimizer integration are tested.
ReLUDown is isolated behind an explicit experimental flag.
/sleep and the CLI sleep action both call DroidEngine.sleep().
Opt-in single worker per Droid with event-based stop/join and configurable idle/interval settings.
Sleep shares the engine lock with teach/recall; cancellation and profile deletion join the worker.
Repeated start calls reuse the single worker; shutdown stops every worker.
Empty store, success, cancellation, concurrent teaching and worker restart are covered.
100-pattern benchmark: 100 distinct expected IDs recovered, coverage 1.0, 160 steps, no expected list passed in.
Pruning quality deltas and schedule stability are measured; the configuration is documented in the task report.
Full suite is green and sleep/MAS state survives profile round trips.
DenseIndex/HNSWIndex implement add/update/delete/rebuild, versioned persistence and exact fallback.
Index candidates feed the existing RRF path without changing recall result fields.
Superseded/deleted facts are filtered and rebuilds are repeatable from the authoritative store.

100k-fact benchmark published on this runner: exact-fallback p50 14.97 ms / p95 17.46 ms with recall@5 1.0 against exact MVM, against the <5 ms target. hnswlib cannot be installed here (no Python.h, no sudo), so the HNSW path stayed unmeasured and the target is not met.
Exact mode preserved; missing dependency, corruption and restart fallbacks are tested.
CrossEncoderReranker scores a bounded candidate set and reports pre/post scores and the scorer used.
Labeled query set: P@5 0.236 -> 0.372 (+57.6% relative) with the lexical fallback scorer; no cross-encoder weights were available.
MatryoshkaAnchor validates 64/384-D projection and the dual index stores both stages with one version.
Migration/re-embedding via DualIndex.migrate; incompatible embeddings raise instead of being truncated; rollback is artifact-based.

64-D first stage measured at 5.96x p50 speedup (target >=6x) with 0.0% relative quality loss (target <=5%) on the declared cluster fixture; an earlier run on the same fixture reported 8.08x. The speedup target is therefore met on one runner and missed on another (2 vCPU, torch 2.6.0 CPU build), so it is not claimed as reproducibly met.
13-model registry with quantization, RAM estimate + source, task tags, provenance URLs and optional speed fields.
Llama 3.2 1B, Qwen2.5 1.5B, SmolLM2 1.7B and Gemma 3 1B carry source-reported values with explicit labels.
recommend(ram_gb, min_tok_s, task) filters hard constraints and returns ranked candidates with rationale and provenance.
Low-RAM, throughput-constrained, reasoning, general-chat, unknown-speed and no-match cases are covered.
Recommended entries map to a GgufBackend config with load_requested False; nothing is downloaded or loaded.
TTC branches by depth, deduplicates, scores with a verifier and enforces candidate/token/time budgets.
The result carries the selected candidate, verifier evidence/score and consumed budget with deterministic ties.
Requires an explicitly identified 8B reference model; no local weights or inference budget in this environment, so no matched-budget comparison was run.
Depends on the 8B reference evaluation; superiority is not claimed without it.
Search never writes memory; persist_selected requires explicit approval and writes exactly one candidate.
Knowledge-store, DroidEngine, profile and checkpoint suites pass (621 passed, 1 skipped).

Lexical exact-match behaviour is covered by the knowledge-store contract tests; the <5 ms at 100k SLA was measured and missed: lexical p50 15.40 ms / p95 16.89 ms on this runner. The exact-match assertions pass, the latency target does not.

Catalog, recommendation and TTC costs are benchmarked with provenance: 13 models with quantization, task tags and source labels (12 of 13 declare unknown throughput rather than inventing a number), recommend() p95 0.09 ms, TTC search p95 0.08 ms over 6 candidates within a 5 s / 8-candidate budget. Generation quality itself needs weights and stays with the blocked 8B evaluation (4.3/4.4).
